statement: On macOS the bundle registers its instance's link scheme (attn-palmac://), not production's attn://, and a link in it reaches that bundle
On Linux the instance's desktop entry handles its own scheme, not production's attn://
Option-modified letter shortcuts (⌥⌘N, the new session dialog's ⌥T, ⌥Q and ⌥1–⌥9) fire through AppKit despite macOS dead-key reporting
A terminal whose pane is no longer drawn detaches from its stream
Hidden tiles release GPU memory and return with one repaint; many tiles never fail
Cell metrics give the same rows and cols as the Tauri build for the same window and font size
On Linux a lone shell tile gets Tauri's 34x106 at 1200x800 and 39x133 at 1440x900
An emoji ZWJ, flag, skin-tone or keycap sequence takes one cell, as grapheme clustering (DECSET 2027) stays on through a program's reset or DECRST
Such a sequence draws as a single glyph on macOS
A Private Use Area icon (Nerd Font) draws from the fonts the native app bundles
It draws on the first frame, with no fallback glyph before the fonts load
Kitty image placements draw where the worker placed them, from pixels pulled once per image, and no client parses kitty escapes
Terminal input latency is measured natively
On Linux the native app gives a lone shell tile the same 9x21 cell, rows and cols as on macOS for the same window
On macOS the native app gives a lone shell tile the same Menlo 9x21 cell, rows and cols as on Linux for the same window
⌘C, from the keyboard or the native Edit menu, copies the terminal's selection
⌘C copies a selected command block's text
⇧⌘C copies the terminal's selection as Markdown, keeping bold, italic, strikethrough, underline and colored inline code
Filter block output lists the block's output lines that hold the query, and a listed line scrolls the view to it
A drag that starts outside the terminal, on its tile's header, paints no selection in it
A program's OSC 52 write reaches the clipboard without a gesture
The terminal's copy and paste reach the system clipboard from the packaged bundle
A spawn link reaches the packaged macOS bundle warm and cold, and starts and shows its agent
A spawn link reaches the native app on Linux
On macOS a link sent while the app runs reaches the running app: a second link for the same folder starts no agent and shows the first
On Linux a link sent while the app runs reaches the running app instead of starting a second one
A terminal mark paints a violet wash and underline over the text it quotes, and only while the rows still read as its quote
A terminal mark brightens while ⌥ is held over it
Terminal marks paint in the packaged app on Linux
